To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

subtle, diffuse disturbance can decouple C and nitrogen cycling in the short term, but that the disturbance-induced changes are small and transient, leading to rapid resilience of C and N cycles in a temperate forest.

a subtle disturbance that accelerated mortality in an aging secondary temperate forest caused a temporary decrease in C allocation to the soil, increased N availability, and increased N uptake by late successional species.

a spatially diffuse experimental disturbance decreased belowground C cycling and caused a short-term decoupling of C and N cycles in a north temperature forest, but that coupled C-N cycles returned to pre-disturbance levels within 2 years.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of subtle disturbance on forest biogeochemistry and how the resulting changes in coupled carbon and nitrogen cycles affect ecosystem resilience.
the resilience of coupled C and N cycling in a north-temperate forest following a disturbance that accelerated the mortality of early-successional canopy dominants.
the role of disturbances in the biogeochemical functioning of forests and how this role may change with forest development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the subtle experimental disturbance decreased belowground carbon allocation, which increased N availability and uptake and accelerated the development of a new, later-successional forest.
the disturbance caused a temporary decoupling between C and N cycling that was followed by resilience of coupled C and N cycling.
subtle disturbance of a forest canopy can alter the balance between C and N cycling, with consequences for forest productivity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
subtle disturbances can have profound effects on ecosystem processes.
subtle disturbance of the early successal canopy in a north temperal forest will result in a short-term decrease of ecosystem C uptake and increase in N leachin.
subtle disturbance can have large impacts on C and N cycling, but that these impacts can be transient.
The main takeaway from our work is that
subtle disturbances can have important, but often subtle and short-lived effects on forest biogeochemistry.
subtle, spatially dispersed disturbances may have different effects on coupled C-N cycling than severe disturbances that kill all trees.
the magnitude of a forest disturbance is a key driver of ecosystem response, and that the effects of subtle disturbances on C and N cycles may be different from the effects of severe disturbances.
